name: Hotel Garuda
summary: A long-running backpacker hotel in Upper Pelling, a few minutes' walk from the jeep stand. Plain, clean rooms, a small restaurant with home-style Sikkimese food, and Kangchenjunga views from the shared terraces on a clear morning.
body: Garuda has been the default first stop for budget travellers in Pelling for years, and for good reason. It sits right in Upper Pelling, so you can step off a shared jeep from Gyalshing, drop your bag and walk to the Sanga Choeling path or the Rabdentse gate without hiring a car. Rooms are simple but kept clean, with geysers and warm blankets in winter.

The kitchen is the quiet strength here. Ask for the Sikkimese thali, a churpi soup or a plate of vegetable momos, and you will eat well for a few hundred rupees. The staff are used to trekkers and solo travellers and will help you find shared cars to Yuksom or Khecheopalri. Online rates can run higher than what you are quoted at the desk in the off-season, so it is worth calling first.
why: Upper Pelling location: walk to the jeep stand, cafés and the Sanga Choeling path
Good, cheap home-style food including a Sikkimese thali
Mountain views from the common terraces at dawn in Oct–Feb
watch_out: It is an older building: some corners look tired, power backup can be limited and the cheaper rooms have no view.

faqs.q: How far is Hotel Garuda from the Pelling jeep stand
faqs.a: It is a few minutes' walk. Shared jeeps from Gyalshing and some direct ones from Siliguri and Gangtok drop passengers in Upper Pelling, and Garuda sits close to that main junction. That is a real saving: you do not need a taxi on arrival, and you can walk to the Sanga Choeling path and the Rabdentse gate on foot.

faqs.q: Do rooms at Hotel Garuda have a Kangchenjunga view
faqs.a: Some upper rooms do, but many budget rooms do not. The good news is that the common terraces face the range, so every guest can step out at sunrise on a clear morning between October and February. If a view from bed matters to you, ask for an upper-floor room when you book and expect to pay a little more.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Garuda good for solo travellers
faqs.a: Yes. It has long been a backpacker favourite, the rooms are cheap, the restaurant is a natural place to meet other travellers, and the staff can point you to shared cars for Yuksom, Khecheopalri or Rinchenpong. Splitting a sightseeing car with two or three people from the hotel can cut your day-trip cost by half or more.

name: Hotel Yangrigang
summary: A plain, friendly hotel on Yuksom's main road, used for years by Goecha La trekkers and pilgrims on the monastery circuit. Close to the jeep stand, the Norbugang walk and the trekking agencies, with a restaurant on site.
body: Yuksom is a small place and most of what you need lies along one road. Yangrigang sits in the middle of it, which makes it handy for trekkers who must collect permits, meet a guide and buy last-minute gloves before the climb to Sachen. Rooms are simple, with attached bathrooms and hot water, and the restaurant serves dal-bhat, thukpa and momos. It is the sort of place where your boots dry by the door and breakfast can be packed the night before.

For non-trekkers it works as a base for two quiet days: the walk to the Norbugang coronation throne and Kathok Lake, the hour's climb to Dubdi Monastery, and a day trip to Tashiding. Book ahead in October and in April–May, when trekking groups fill Yuksom; outside those months you can often walk in and ask. Rates here stay modest even in season, so it suits travellers who would rather spend on a guide or a good porter than on a fancy room. Pay in cash where you can.
why: Main-road location close to the jeep stand and trekking agencies
Walking distance to Norbugang, Kathok Lake and the Dubdi trail
Budget rates and a restaurant that is used to early trek starts
watch_out: Rooms are basic and Yuksom has occasional power cuts and patchy mobile data, so carry a torch and download maps before you arrive.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Yangrigang a good base for the Goecha La trek
faqs.a: Yes, for the nights before and after the trek. It is on the main road near the trekking agencies and the forest checkpost, so collecting permits and meeting your guide is easy. Ask the hotel to keep your extra luggage while you are on the trail; most Yuksom hotels do this, but confirm it when you book.

faqs.q: Can I walk to Norbugang from Hotel Yangrigang
faqs.a: Yes. The Norbugang park with the coronation throne, the chorten and the Kathok Lake loop are all within an easy walk of the main road, roughly 10 to 20 minutes depending on where you start. Go early in the morning when the village is quiet and the light on the old cryptomeria above the throne is soft.

faqs.q: When should I book Yuksom hotels in advance
faqs.a: Book ahead for October, the busiest trekking month, and for April–May when rhododendrons bring trekkers and school-holiday families. In December–February and in the monsoon months Yuksom is quiet and you can usually walk in and bargain. Even then, call a day ahead if you will arrive after dark, because some hotels close their gates early.

name: Sherpa Lodge
rate_band: ₹1,800–3,500 per room night, meals often extra or bundled, indicative
summary: A family-run lodge in Okhrey, the Sherpa village that serves as the base for the Hilley–Barsey rhododendron walk. Wood-panelled rooms, mountain views on clear days, home-cooked food and hosts who can arrange the drive to Hilley.
body: Okhrey's homestays grew out of the rhododendron season, when walkers come for the Hilley–Barsey trail between March and May. Sherpa Lodge is one of the established places here, run by a Sherpa family, with wood-panelled rooms that stay warm on cold nights and a dining room where dinner is whatever the kitchen cooked that evening: rice, dal, a local green, perhaps a chicken curry, and tea on tap.

The value is in the arrangements as much as the room. The family can book a car for the 30-minute run to Hilley, tell you which days the sanctuary trail is crowded, and point you to the village monastery for an evening walk. Expect simple comforts, a bucket of hot water when the geyser struggles, and a quiet you will not find in Pelling. Bring a torch and a book.
why: Base for the Hilley–Barsey walk, about 30 minutes by road from Hilley
Home-cooked meals and a family that arranges local transport
Far cheaper and quieter than staying in Pelling during rhododendron season
watch_out: It is a village homestay: hot water and electricity can be patchy, and in peak bloom weeks (late March–April) rooms fill fast.

faqs.q: How do I reach Sherpa Lodge in Okhrey
faqs.a: From Siliguri take a shared jeep or SNT bus to Jorethang, then a shared jeep towards Sombaria and Okhrey; the whole run is about 130 km and 5–6 hours. A reserved car from NJP costs far more but saves the change at Jorethang. Ask the lodge to confirm the last jeep timings, which change with the season.

faqs.q: Is Okhrey better than Hilley for the Barsey walk
faqs.a: Okhrey has more homestays and a proper village around you, while Hilley is the actual trailhead. Most people stay in Okhrey, drive 30 minutes to Hilley early, walk 4 km to Barsey and return the same day or stay a night at the Guras Kunj hut. Okhrey gives you more choice of rooms and food.

faqs.q: When is the best time to stay in Okhrey
faqs.a: Mid-March to late April for the rhododendron bloom on the Barsey ridge, and October to December for clear views of Kangchenjunga and the Singalila range. January and February are cold but quiet and cheap. The monsoon months, June to September, bring leeches, cloud and slippery village roads.

name: Mt. Narsing Village Resort
summary: An old favourite about 4 km from Ravangla on the Gangtok–Pelling road, in two parts: a cheaper roadside wing and an upper annexe of cottages with lawns and views of Mount Narsing, Kabru and the Rangit valley.
body: Mt. Narsing Village Resort has hosted travellers on the Gangtok–Pelling road for a long time, well before the Buddha Park made Ravangla famous. The roadside wing is simple and cheaper; the annexe, about a kilometre up the hill, has cottage rooms set around open lawns, and that is where we would put families and couples who want the view. Families like the space; there is room for children to run on the grass and for older travellers to sit out in the sun.

On a clear morning between October and February the peaks of Narsing and Kabru stand over the valley, and the monasteries of South and West Sikkim dot the ridges below. The kitchen serves Sikkimese, Indian and Chinese dishes. You will want a car for the Buddha Park, Ralang and the Temi tea garden, all within a short drive. Drives are short: Ravangla town is about 4 km away and Ralang about 10 km. Ask for an annexe room with a view when you book.
why: Upper annexe cottages with lawns and wide mountain views
Handy stop on the Gangtok–Pelling road, about 4 km from Ravangla
Two wings mean a choice between budget and comfort rooms
watch_out: It is out of town, so you need a car or a walk on the highway to reach Ravangla's shops and the Buddha Park, and the roadside wing is plainer than the annexe.

faqs.q: Which wing of Mt. Narsing Village Resort should I book
faqs.a: Book the upper annexe if you want views and quiet: its cottage rooms sit around lawns about a kilometre above the road and look out over Narsing, Kabru and the Rangit valley. The roadside wing is cheaper and fine for a one-night halt on the Gangtok–Pelling road, but the setting is plainer and you will hear traffic.

faqs.q: How far is Mt. Narsing Village Resort from the Buddha Park
faqs.a: The resort is about 4 km from Ravangla town and the Buddha Park lies just beyond the town, so it is a short drive of roughly 10–15 minutes. Walking is possible but the route follows the highway, which is not pleasant after dark. Ask the resort to arrange a local car for a half-day loop with Ralang Monastery.

faqs.q: Is Ravangla a good overnight stop between Gangtok and Pelling
faqs.a: Yes. Gangtok to Pelling is about 120 km and five hours of mountain road, and a night in Ravangla breaks it neatly in two. You get the Buddha Park and Ralang Monastery the same afternoon, a dawn view of the range, and a shorter, easier drive to Pelling the next morning.

name: Cherry Resort
image_query: Cherry Resort Temi Tea Garden Sikkim
summary: A three-storey hotel inside the Temi tea estate, built by the state tourism corporation as the Yatri Niwas and now run privately on lease. Rooms look over the tea slopes and the Teesta gorge, and Himalayan cherry trees line the approach road.
body: There are not many places in Sikkim where you can wake up in the middle of a working tea garden. Cherry Resort is one of them. The building belongs to the Sikkim Tourism Development Corporation and was once its Yatri Niwas; it is now leased out and run privately under the name taken from the Himalayan cherry trees that flower along the drive from November.

Most rooms face the estate, with pickers on the slopes in the morning during the flush seasons and Kangchenjunga on the skyline on clear winter days. It is a calm base for a slow day: a walk through the garden, a visit to the factory gate for fresh Temi tea, and an easy drive to Namchi or Ravangla. Evenings are very quiet, so bring a book; dinner is served in the hotel's own dining room.
why: Inside the Temi tea estate, with garden walks from the door
Cherry blossom on the approach road in November
Central for Namchi, Ravangla and the Tendong area
watch_out: It is a government-built block rather than a heritage bungalow, the finish can feel dated, and evening food choices are limited to the in-house kitchen.

faqs.q: Is Cherry Resort inside the Temi Tea Garden
faqs.a: Yes. It stands on the slopes of the Temi estate, the Sikkim government's tea garden set up in 1969, so the tea bushes start right outside. You can walk the estate roads in the morning and buy packets of Temi tea at the outlet near the factory. Ask at reception about the day's factory timings.

faqs.q: When do the cherry trees flower at Temi
faqs.a: The Himalayan cherry that lines the approach road flowers in late autumn, usually through November, which is unusual for a cherry and a good reason to plan a Sikkim trip that month. Clear skies in November also give the best chance of seeing Kangchenjunga from the estate. Exact bloom weeks shift a little each year.

faqs.q: How far is Cherry Resort from Namchi and Ravangla
faqs.a: Both are close: Namchi is roughly 16–20 km and Ravangla about the same, each 45 minutes to an hour by road. That makes the resort a good middle base for a South Sikkim loop of Samdruptse, Char Dham, the Buddha Park and Ralang. Gangtok is around 60 km away, about two and a half hours.

name: Norbu Ghang Resort
summary: One of Pelling's older resorts, open since 1999: brick cottages with carved eaves in terraced gardens on the edge of town, larger pine-panelled suites facing the snows, and a spa known for the traditional Sikkimese hot stone bath.
body: Norbu Ghang was among the first resorts in Pelling built with Sikkimese design in mind rather than as a concrete block. The cottages sit on terraces planted with rhododendron and orchids, each with a small verandah, and the suites are oriented towards Kangchenjunga. On a clear October morning that verandah is where you will want your first cup of tea. It has kept a calmer, older feel than the newer hotels in the centre of town.

The spa offers the hot stone bath, in which river stones heated in a fire are dropped into a wooden tub, a soak locals take for aches after long walks. The resort is a short drive from Pemayangtse and Rabdentse. It is a step up from the town hotels in space and calm, though some fittings show their age. Ask for a recently refurbished room, and book directly in the off-season to ask about meal-inclusive rates.
why: Cottages with private verandahs facing the range
Traditional hot stone bath at the spa
Quiet edge-of-town setting, a short drive from Pemayangtse
watch_out: As with many Pelling properties, the finish does not always match the price, so ask for a renovated cottage or a suite with a direct view.

faqs.q: What is the hot stone bath at Norbu Ghang
faqs.a: It is a traditional Sikkimese soak. River stones are heated in a fire and dropped into a wooden tub of water with herbs, warming it slowly and, people say, easing sore muscles. It is especially welcome after the Sanga Choeling climb or a cold dawn at the viewpoint. Book it at the spa a few hours ahead; it is charged separately.

faqs.q: Do all rooms at Norbu Ghang face Kangchenjunga
faqs.a: Not all. The suites and many cottages are set up for the view, but some rooms face the gardens or the valley. If seeing the range from your verandah is the point of the trip, ask for a suite or a named view cottage when booking, and come between October and February when the sky is clearest.

faqs.q: Is Norbu Ghang walking distance from Pelling town
faqs.a: It is on the outskirts, so you can walk to the town centre but most guests use a car for sightseeing. Pemayangtse and the Rabdentse gate are a short drive away. The edge-of-town position is the trade-off: fewer cafés on the doorstep, but quieter nights and wider views than the hotels on the main road.

name: The Elgin Mount Pandim
summary: A heritage hotel opposite Pemayangtse Monastery, set in about eight acres of forest and gardens below Pelling. The Elgin group says it was built by the Chogyal as a royal retreat. Quiet, old-fashioned comfort with the range across the valley.
body: The Mount Pandim sits on the ridge facing Pemayangtse, one of Sikkim's oldest monasteries, a short walk across the road. The Elgin group, which also runs historic hotels in Darjeeling and Gangtok, describes the building as a former royal retreat of Sikkim's ruling family. Today it is the most traditional of Pelling's premium stays: wood floors, a tea lounge, a bar and a dining room that serves Sikkimese dishes alongside the usual menu.

Rooms look across to the snows and down to the valleys, and the gardens and surrounding forest are good for birds in the early morning. You are a little away from Pelling's market, which suits people who want the monastery and the mountains more than the cafés. The Sanga Choeling ridge and the Rabdentse ruins are short drives away, and the hotel can arrange cars for the Yuksom and Khecheopalri road. It suits slow travellers who want two or three quiet nights, early walks to the monastery and long breakfasts with the mountains in view. Book well ahead for October and the Christmas holidays.
why: Directly opposite Pemayangtse Monastery: walk to morning prayers
Gardens and forest grounds, good for birds and quiet
Heritage character that the newer Pelling hotels lack
watch_out: It sits below the town on the Pemayangtse road, so you need a car for Upper Pelling's cafés, and older heritage rooms can feel cold in winter until the heater runs.

faqs.q: How close is the Elgin Mount Pandim to Pemayangtse Monastery
faqs.a: It is directly opposite, a short walk away. That is the hotel's greatest asset: you can walk over for early prayers, when the monastery is quiet and the light is soft, and be back for breakfast. Rabdentse ruins are also close by road. Check monastery timings with the hotel, as they shift during festivals.

faqs.q: Is the Elgin Mount Pandim worth the price
faqs.a: If you value a quiet heritage setting, gardens and a monastery on your doorstep, yes. If you want a modern spa resort or to be in the middle of Pelling's market, the newer properties in town may suit you better. Off-season months, especially June to September and January, bring noticeably lower rates.

faqs.q: Can you see Kangchenjunga from the Elgin Mount Pandim
faqs.a: Yes, on clear days the range rises across the valley, and October to February gives the best odds. Mornings are clearest; by late morning in spring the haze often closes in. For the classic sunrise colour, set an alarm, wrap up warm and watch from the garden before breakfast.

name: The Chumbi Mountain Retreat & Spa
summary: A modern resort at Naku Chumbong in Lower Pelling, laid out like a Sikkimese monastery in stone and carved wood, with a spa, several restaurants and balconies facing the range. Pelling's most complete resort for couples and families.
body: The Chumbi was built in local style rather than as a glass box: stone walls, earth tones and hand-carved woodwork, with buildings arranged in the manner of a monastery around courtyards. Rooms have balconies, and the better ones look straight at the Kangchenjunga range. It is a Club Mahindra associate property, so expect families in school holidays. Grounds spread over several acres of terraced slope.

Most guests use it as a place to slow down between sightseeing runs: Pemayangtse and Rabdentse are a short drive, Khecheopalri and Yuksom make a full day, and the spa is there when you come back cold and tired. Food is the most varied in Pelling, from Sikkimese dishes to the standard multi-cuisine buffet. Ask for a room on the upper levels for the clearest view of the range.
why: Monastery-inspired architecture in stone and carved wood
Full spa and several dining options under one roof
Balconies facing the range from the view rooms
watch_out: It is in Lower Pelling, a drive from the Upper Pelling cafés, and it gets busy and noisier with families in May–June and the Puja holidays.

faqs.q: Is The Chumbi Mountain Retreat good for a honeymoon
faqs.a: Yes, it is one of the most popular honeymoon choices in West Sikkim: view rooms with balconies, a spa, several restaurants and enough space to feel private. For a quieter stay, avoid the school-holiday weeks of May–June and the Puja holidays in October, and ask for a room on an upper level facing the range.

faqs.q: Where is The Chumbi Mountain Retreat in Pelling
faqs.a: It is at Naku Chumbong in Lower Pelling, below the main town. Pemayangtse Monastery and the Rabdentse ruins are a short drive away, and Upper Pelling's market and cafés are about 10–15 minutes by car. Most guests keep a car for the day, since walking back uphill at night is not pleasant.

faqs.q: When are rates lowest at The Chumbi
faqs.a: Rates usually drop in the monsoon, June to September, and in January–February outside the New Year week. Views are less reliable in the monsoon, but January and February are cold, clear and quiet. Booking directly and asking about meal-inclusive packages can save money over adding meals at the restaurant.

name: Yangsum Heritage Farm
rate_band: ₹7,000–12,000 per room night with meals, indicative
summary: A family farmhouse on a 44-acre organic farm near Rinchenpong, with an old house remodelled in the 1960s, Tibetan-style wood-panelled rooms and meals cooked from what grows on the land. Slow, personal and far from Pelling's traffic.
body: Yangsum is a working farm first and a guesthouse second, which is exactly its charm. The family house dates back to the 1800s and was remodelled in 1966; rooms are wood-panelled in Tibetan style with attached bathrooms. Around it, the land runs through cardamom, oranges, avocados, vegetables and patches of mixed forest with alder, chestnut, magnolia and rhododendron. Guests are welcome to walk the land and see what is in season.

Days are simple: breakfast from the farm, a walk to the Rinchenpong monastery and its rare Ati Buddha image, an afternoon on forest trails or with the farm work, and a Sikkimese dinner in the evening. Kangchenjunga rises across the valley on clear mornings. It costs more than a village homestay because meals, space and hosting are part of the stay. Book directly and well ahead.
why: A real family farm with home-grown, organic meals
Wood-panelled rooms in an old Sikkimese farmhouse
Walks to Rinchenpong monastery and Kaluk's viewpoints
watch_out: It is remote by design: you need a car to get there, evenings are quiet with little nightlife, and rooms are few, so book well ahead.

faqs.q: How do I get to Yangsum Heritage Farm
faqs.a: Yangsum lies near Rinchenpong in Soreng district, about 40 km and 1.5–2 hours from Pelling or roughly 5 hours by road from Siliguri. A reserved car is the easy option. Budget travellers can take a shared jeep to Rinchenpong or Kaluk from Jorethang or Gyalshing and ask the farm to collect them; confirm timings ahead.

faqs.q: Are meals included at Yangsum Heritage Farm
faqs.a: Most stays are booked with meals, and the food is a big part of the experience: breakfast and dinner made largely from the farm's own produce, Sikkimese in style. Rinchenpong has few restaurants, so plan to eat at the farm. Mention dietary needs when you book, as the kitchen cooks for a small number of guests.

faqs.q: What is there to do around Yangsum Heritage Farm
faqs.a: Walk the farm and its forest trails, visit Rinchenpong Monastery (built in 1730) with its Ati Buddha image, watch sunrise over Kangchenjunga from the Kaluk side, and hear the local tradition of the poisoned pond. Day trips reach Pelling, the Singshore Bridge and Uttarey. Most guests stay two or three nights and slow down.
